explanation: Heidi looks with 'wondering eyes,' screams aloud at the picture, and 'devoured the scene' with 'glowing eyes,' all signs of delight and fascination. Her scream is excitement, not fear, so C misreads it, and nothing suggests she was upset beforehand (A) or had never seen a shepherd (D).

The text contrasts the tragedies, whose broad themes still appeal to modern audiences, with the history plays, which may require deep knowledge of English history. The logical consequence is that today's readers and theatergoers likely find the history plays less engaging, as A says. The other choices introduce comparisons the text never sets up, such as twentieth-century plays or the preferences of history experts.

The narrator describes a walking trip and admits that the winding path left him unsure of the direction to the village, meaning he got lost. B and C add ideas (fond memories, a frequently visited place) not in the text, and D is wrong because the text never says how he solved the problem.

Earlier estimates (297 and 344 km/s) were low enough for the LMC to stay in orbit, while the 2006 estimate of 378 km/s is too high, according to Besla. So the maximum velocity allowing orbit must lie above 344 km/s and below 378 km/s. B is tempting but ignores that 344 km/s was still low enough for orbit, so the limit must be higher than that.

The claim is that endothermy let mosasaurs live in cold polar waters. If many mosasaur fossils are found near the Cretaceous poles but few fossils of nonendothermic reptiles are, that suggests endothermy gave mosasaurs an advantage in cold waters. B shows no difference between the groups, and D suggests polar waters were warm, which weakens the need for endothermy.

The text asks 'What explains its rise in popularity?' and then answers: 'y'all' always refers to more than one person, so it is more precise than 'you.' That is a question about why the word has spread in the US. The text gives no counts of other plural forms, no first recorded use, and no information about other countries.

The student claims Catlett was good at unifying different artistic traditions. A describes her combining an ancient Indigenous technique with the styles of Mexican muralists and a German artist, which is exactly that. The other quotations describe her works or subjects but don't show multiple traditions being blended.

The ecosystem view says conservation works better when it accounts for interactions among climate, terrain, and other species. If that is right, focusing only on M. boolii would miss how other species in Sonora affect its survival, as D says. C is tempting, but a single-species approach focuses more on M. boolii, not less.

The student says the notes were added mainly to help sell the volume. If the publishers asked for the notes specifically to make the book attractive to readers who already owned the poem, that directly shows a marketing motive. B is about critics' opinions of the notes' effect on the poem, not why the notes were included.

Herding means peer countries freely imitate each other and converge on the same rate regardless of circumstances. If African countries had their accumulation policies set individually by economic unions, they couldn't converge by imitation, while the Asian countries, free to choose, could. The other choices describe differences in reserves or crisis effects that don't explain why imitation would appear in one region and not the other.
The study with the most participants is the Ghana and Kenya study with 142 participants, and its population was adolescents only. B describes the India study, which had 94 participants, not the most.

The text explains that the Wigner crystal was mostly conjecture until 2021, when researchers captured an image of it, the first visual confirmation. So the main idea is that researchers now have the strongest evidence yet that the crystal exists. B is too general, and C overstates graphene's role, which is only one detail of the method.

In A, Alexandra hears insects as 'the sweetest music' and feels as if her heart were hiding in the grass among the wild creatures, which shows a deep emotional bond with nature. B and D show her practical farming knowledge, and C describes a drive through the dark without expressing feelings about the land.

The predicted psychological effect is that positive feedback improves how people feel about the exercise; the predicted physical effect is better endurance. D shows positive-feedback participants enjoyed the task more but kept their heart and pedaling rates for about the same time as others, so the psychological effect appeared but the physical one didn't. The other choices either don't isolate the positive-feedback group or don't show the enjoyment-without-endurance pattern.

The farmers used Haudenosaunee techniques but mostly hadn't seen Haudenosaunee farms, and the text rules out independent invention. The remaining explanation is that they learned the techniques secondhand from people with more direct exposure. The other choices don't address how the farmers acquired the techniques.

The saying that the doctor carries more family secrets than any archbishop, and the image of secrets staying 'nicely bottled up' rather than flying out like parrots, show that he keeps confidences. So people likely don't worry he will reveal them. The hat is described humorously, but nothing suggests people merely tolerate him (A) or that he discusses his own family (C).

Tannen's hypothesis is that a debate format is less informative than presenting multiple perspectives noncompetitively. If viewers of the panel (several noncompetitive views) answered more questions correctly than viewers of the debate, that supports her. A and B measure perceived knowledge of commentators, not how informed the audience became, and D doesn't involve the multi-perspective panel.

Businesses assume interruptions hurt productivity, but Puranik's team found that interruptions by colleagues can boost belonging and job satisfaction. So businesses should recognize that these social benefits may offset the perceived costs. B goes too far by recommending frequent interruptions, and D contradicts the research.

Microplastics were found even in layers older than their invention because they migrated downward. That means the deepest layer containing microplastics doesn't mark when they first appeared, so it can't mark the start of the Anthropocene. B is a trap: the microplastics in old layers didn't come from that era, so they say nothing against 1950.

If Henry had a survey of the value of church holdings done quickly in the year just before the Dissolution, that suggests he was focused on the monasteries' wealth, supporting a financial motive. D links the Dissolution to economic hardship for others, not to Henry's motive, and A and B don't speak to why the policy was enacted.

In 1973 about 74% of House members and 79% of senators were veterans; by 2013 both were under 20%, a substantial decrease in both houses. A is wrong because the Senate was higher in 2003, B fails because both were below 50% by 2003, and D ignores the big drop from 1993 to 2013.

Ecologists learn about wild-bee declines mostly from bumblebees, but bumblebees have uncommon traits (sociality and dietary generalism) that make them more resilient to some changes. So their responses may not match those of other wild bees, and researchers should be careful generalizing from them, as D says. B goes too far by ruling out even similar bees, and C makes a prediction the text doesn't support.

The graph shows the low-anger review rated slightly more helpful than the no-anger control, while the high-anger review was rated less helpful. That matches both parts of the conclusion: some anger doesn't hurt perceptions of the review, but a lot of anger does. D compares only low and high anger and leaves out the control, so it can't show that the mere presence of anger is harmless.

The poem compares a lion with an untamed heart to a man with a 'lofty soul in dreams and visions wrapped' who is 'in the stifling flesh securely trapped.' That describes people whose aspirations are held back by limitations. The poem says nothing about taming animals, motivation, or self-control.

At every depth, beach-shell tools outnumber seafloor-shell tools (e.g., 99 vs. 33 at 3–4 meters), which suggests seafloor shells were harder to get. C contradicts the text, which says beach shells are thin and eroded, not durable. B and D don't address how hard the shells were to obtain.

In A, Whitman tells readers 'You have not known what you are' and says they have slumbered on themselves, directly saying they haven't understood themselves. D says no one else has understood the reader, which is about others' understanding, not the reader's own.

The species were known only from fossil bones more than 55 million years old and are described as 'previously unknown' prehistoric penguins, so they no longer exist. C contradicts the text, since one species was over three times the size of today's largest penguin.

At current temperatures about 82% of sites can meet 0% of heating needs with thermal pollution; at the maximum plausible temperature, that falls to about 14%. So far more sites could use thermal pollution as temperatures rise. C is tempting, but only about 78% of sites (not more than 80%) exceed 25% at the maximum temperature, and A wrongly says those sites meet all their needs.

The number of department leaders reporting to the CEO rose from about 3.3 to 4 to about 6.8 across the three periods, showing CEOs connecting with more departments over time. C is true but only compares leaders with managers and doesn't show a growing trend.

Armijo predicts that more heliostats will cut solar roasting time. The fastest batch with 38–42 heliostats took six minutes, so a batch with 50 heliostats taking less than six minutes directly supports this. The other choices concern evenness, flavor, or peeling, not speed.

The finding is that bulkheads are more strongly tied to low waterbird community integrity than riprap. A bulkhead-heavy site (Old Road) scoring lower than a riprap-heavy site (Miles) illustrates that directly. C compares hardened vs. unhardened shorelines without separating bulkheads from riprap.

Dipoles normally can't synchronize at higher temperatures, but the researchers propose that polarons shield dipoles from thermal interference, allowing superfluorescence at room temperature. So polarons let the dipoles synchronize despite the heat. The text doesn't say polarons change burst speed, intensity, or movement between materials.

In D, Alexandra watches the stars and thinks about their 'ordered march'; reflecting on the laws behind nature 'fortified her' and gave her 'a sense of personal security.' That is comfort drawn from understanding the world. B shows emotional attachment to the land but not comfort from understanding it, and A shows her bracing for something painful.
The table lists 14.22 percent for games first released in 1995–1999. The 1985–1989 figure is 15.38 percent, and 1970–1974 and 2000–2004 don't appear in the table at all.

The graph shows extra electricity generated when winds were stronger than forecast, and the West bar reaches about 150 thousand MWh. D uses the Midwest's value (about 175 thousand), and B and C wrongly describe weak winds, which the graph isn't about.

The highest percentage of bus stops with shaded shelter in any area is 29%, in the 125.6° area. That low maximum supports the claim that all areas need more shade. 15% is the lowest value, and 50% and 90% aren't in the table.

Polynesian sweet potatoes split from South American ones over 100,000 years ago, but people have lived in Polynesia only for about 3,000 years. So the plant must have arrived without human help, as C says. B contradicts the DNA evidence, and A isn't supported because the text discusses when varieties diverged, not when cultivation began.

Tanks with the rooted underwater plant watermilfoil released less methane than tanks with duckweed or algae. That suggests underwater plants like watermilfoil help keep methane from escaping. The study didn't compare shallow and deep water (B), and D's mix of plants was never tested.

The claim is that the book encouraged Latina authors to write fiction about their own youth. Latina authors saying the book inspired them to write about their own adolescence is direct support. B involves authors who are not Latina, and C and D show popularity or comparisons, not influence on authors' choices.

The text says archaeologists hope to use scent to better understand ancient rituals, trade, social hierarchies, and medicine, which are important aspects of ancient life. D twists the mention of medicine: they want to understand ancient medicine, not create new drugs.

Every ecotype grew equally well in every water sample, and zinc helped all of them, so the water itself didn't reveal any local adaptation. Since light and temperature weren't replicated, any adaptations could still exist but would concern conditions other than the water, as C says. A is too strong because the study didn't test those other conditions, and B contradicts the finding that zinc affected all ecotypes the same way.

The text stresses that Zelda wrote a novel and many short stories of her own. Seeing her mainly as F. Scott's inspiration ignores that work, so such people risk misrepresenting her full contribution to literature. A is about F. Scott's motivations, which the text doesn't discuss.

The underlined claim says the grid-cell-like behavior comes from the networks' programmed rules rather than any real resemblance to brains. If those rules have no equivalent in biological brains, then the behavior reflects the programming, not brain-like organization. B concerns networks that did not show grid-cell behavior, so it doesn't explain the ones that did.

From 2011/2012 to 2012/2013, Argentina's exports fell from about 81% to about 70%, but it stayed well above Brazil (about 31%) and the US (about 7%). A is wrong because Brazil decreased and was above the US, B fails because Brazil never exceeded Argentina, and D is wrong because 2012/2013 was the US's lowest point.

The text says Siemomysł's 'historical actuality is disputed' and that his record relies on oral tradition, while Mieszko II Lambert is presented as a documented king. So historians accept that Mieszko existed but disagree about Siemomysł. D is wrong because the oral tradition concerns Siemomysł, not Mieszko.

At 48 hours, about 73% of seeds treated with 10 micromoles per liter had germinated, compared with about 50% of untreated seeds, showing faster germination. A only describes treated seeds and doesn't compare with untreated ones, D misreads the values, and C misstates the graph, since 500-micromole seeds reached only about 85%.

Sediment makes rivers look yellow, which the researchers defined as wavelengths of 560 nm and above. If segments flowing into lakes were mostly above 560 nm and those flowing out were mostly below, that shows inflowing segments carry more sediment. C doesn't compare inflowing and outflowing segments, and B is about the lakes themselves.

Harvey Danger earned less than expected because most listeners paid nothing, while Jane Siberry earned a lot because many listeners paid extra. These opposite outcomes suggest the model works well for some musicians and poorly for others. B overgeneralizes from one band and one solo artist, and the text says nothing about popularity or lowering prices.
'We shall never know defeat' looks ahead and predicts success. C describes something already done ('We have answered'), and A and B are a question and an invitation rather than predictions.

Manzoor's survey linked background music to customers' enjoyment, and the text discusses why the music reduced enjoyment for some shoppers. So the study asked how background music affects the shopping experience. The text mentions nothing about volume, money spent online versus in stores, or music genres.

Anterior (head) genes were active across the whole sea star body, while posterior genes appeared only at the edges and trunk genes aren't mentioned as active. That suggests sea stars are basically all head with no trunk, rather than having lost their head as assumed. B contradicts the known bilateral origin the text accepts, and A and C aren't supported by the gene pattern.

The claim is that as the movement spread beyond Chile, it drew on a wider range of musical traditions. Songs showing the influence of corrido, a Mexican genre, show a non-Chilean tradition entering the movement. C is tempting, but the quena is already used in Chile, so it doesn't show expansion, and D is about where artists worked, not the traditions they used.

The text contrasts a ground-based, knuckle-walking origin with new observations of orangutans standing on two legs in trees to reach fruit. That points to a different possibility: bipedalism may have arisen because it helped a tree-dwelling ancestor. D still assumes a knuckle-walking ancestor, which the observations are meant to challenge, and B and C aren't supported.

While the stories were copyrighted, adapters had to pay a fee and get approval from strict copyright holders. With copyright over, those barriers are gone, so making adaptations becomes easier and cheaper, which explains the predicted increase. The other choices don't follow from the end of copyright.

The researchers suggest NFM lowers voting indirectly, meaning through some other factor. If NFM strongly lowers political knowledge and interest, and those are strongly tied to voting, then NFM would reduce voting through them. C says NFM has little link to knowledge or interest, which breaks the chain, and D doesn't show NFM lowering knowledge.

In C, she reminds her husband to care for the cat, birds, and flowers and to look after himself, showing concern for things at home in Seattle. The other quotations describe her activities and plans in California.

The team concluded that certain soil microbes might explain why some plants stayed healthy. Finding more microbes that inhibit the disease-causing bacteria around healthy plants directly supports that. C points to moisture rather than microbes, and D suggests microbes made no difference.

The text says Mother wrote stories for the children and made up funny poems for birthdays and other occasions. A contradicts the text's description of 'dull' visits, and B and D claim favorites the text never names.

Campfires typically reach above 400°C, so artifacts exposed to such temperatures support control of fire. The graph shows L5_239 at about 550°C and K3_18 at about 650°C. A is wrong because K5_106 and K3_9 were only around 150–200°C, and C's 100°C threshold is too low to indicate fire.

The wet and warm scenario means liquid water lasted a long time. A basin showing an ancient ocean with gradual sea-level changes over an extended period fits that directly. C supports the opposite view of a brief melting event, and A and D don't tell us how long water was present.

D describes 'a certain sense of detachment from ordinary day and daylight duties,' which is exactly an escape from everyday life. B praises the journey's stops and C mentions seclusion in a berth, but neither speaks of leaving daily routines behind.
La Torre 6B's footprint is 28.9 cm, shorter than 6A's 32.8 cm, and its average stride is 5.57 m, longer than 6A's 5.23 m. So the faster theropod had a shorter footprint and a longer stride.

Mahtta et al. say GDP growth should matter more to land expansion as governments become more efficient. In Region 1, GDP's share fell from about 38% (1970–2000) to about 26% (2000–2014), which suggests governments there became less efficient. Region 2's GDP share rose sharply, so D is wrong about Region 1, and C's claim about individual countries can't be read from regional averages.

The tool similarities could come from imitation or trade, but the team found genetic links among the settlements' populations. That raises another possibility: the similar tools came from populations mixing. A, C, and D add claims about timing, direction of imitation, or other cultural differences that the text doesn't support.

The discovery matters because no nesting sites were previously known in northern South America, which led scientists to think titanosaurs migrated south to lay eggs. That implies this site is farther north than other known South American nesting sites. The text gives no information about it being the earliest site, about excavation difficulty, or about other sauropods.

Studying philosophy builds knowledge of foundational texts and figures; doing philosophy applies that expertise creatively, treating past figures as 'vital interlocutors' who help produce new insights. That is B: new ideas through a kind of dialogue with past philosophers, built on knowledge gained from studying. A's 'practical issues' clashes with the text's abstract questions about existence, and C's emphasis on challenging ideas isn't stated.
In the table, the row for dolphin FB43 lists a recording year of 1992. The year 2012 belongs to FB07, and 1999 and 2020 don't appear in the table.

The researchers say the unprotected reef has far fewer top-level predators because fishing is allowed there. If fishers disproportionately remove top-trophic species, then fishing would cut exactly that share of biomass, linking the difference to regulatory status. C suggests Bajos del Norte would be fished less, which works against the explanation, and A and B don't connect the difference to fishing.

Nestlings preferred their local dialect, and song preference affects mate choice. So as adults they will likely choose mates from their own local population, as C says. A contradicts the role of preference in mate selection, and B and D bring in food amounts and other species, which the study didn't examine.

Zheng argues that the world music label lumps very different traditions into one category. If mbaqanga and quan họ developed separately and have little in common, yet both get called world music, the label clearly erases real differences. D says they are similar to each other, which would make grouping them reasonable and weaken her claim.

Processing with assembly needs no capital, while processing with inputs requires firms to spend capital on materials. From 2000 to 2006, inputs imports rose from about 650 to 2,300, much faster than assembly imports (about 250 to 750), suggesting firms gained enough capital to favor the capital-intensive type. A is false because ordinary imports were still the largest in 2006, and C doesn't show any change in firms' capital.

A good control group must be people similar to office-holders who just don't hold office, but researchers can't decide who wins elections. So they will have trouble finding such a well-matched control group. C recommends the opposite of what the text says is needed, and A and B aren't supported.

The text says the orchestra performs classical music and, through iConduct!, lets community members learn and try conducting the orchestra. That means people can both listen to and take part in performances. B is too narrow, since Montgomery is only one example, and D gives a reason for iConduct! that the text never states.

A shorter cell lifetime means cells must be replaced more often. If buying new materials costs more than recycling, each extra replacement widens the cost gap between plants using new cells and those using recycled cells, so the LCOE difference grows. D blames operating costs, which would affect both kinds of plants and wouldn't explain the growing gap, and B doesn't compare the two types.

People who touched the items were willing to pay much more than those who couldn't. Since touching is possible in stores but not online, in-person shopping may make products seem more valuable. D reverses the logic, because online shoppers can't touch products, and A and C go beyond the findings.

If only common factors drove the rise, the increase should look similar across countries. But from 1970 to 2000, men's median marriage age in England and Wales rose about 5 years (30 to 35), compared with about 2–3 years in the US, so something country-specific likely contributed. C describes a difference in levels that existed throughout the century, not a difference in how the increase happened.

Asiedu finds that more resource dependence goes with less foreign investment, which seems surprising since extraction needs large investments, and explains it by the instability boom-bust cycles create, which investors dislike. C captures both the unexpected pattern and its cause. A gives the wrong cause, and B and D misstate the relationship.

The claim is that putting a work online increases how many people experience it. If more people view the online image of Mississippi Delta each year than visit the museum in person, the online version clearly reaches more people. The other choices are about the museum's collection or the work's reputation, not its audience size.

In C, the narrator says she has traveled a lot and enjoyed it, but never more than her trips within her native town, which directly compares her hometown favorably with other places. A, B, and D praise the town but don't compare it with anywhere else.

B says that whenever Marianne and Willoughby disagreed about books, the disagreement lasted only until 'the force of her arguments and the brightness of her eyes' won him over, which shows her persuading him that her taste is right. D shows they already agreed, so no persuasion was needed, and A and C show her interest, not her persuasiveness.
